title: Alans
capsule: The Alans were an Iranic nomadic people, related to the Sarmatians and speaking an ancestor of modern Ossetian, who crossed the Rhine with Vandals and Suebi in 406 CE. On entering Iberia in 409 they settled in Lusitania and Hispania Carthaginensis, constituting a small warrior elite among millions of Hispano-Romans. Their king Addac was killed in battle against the Visigoths in 418, and the surviving Alans, now leaderless, accepted subordination under the Hasding Vandal king Gunderic, who adopted the title Rex Wandalorum et Alanorum. The Alan remnant crossed with the Vandals into North Africa in 429, ending any distinct Iberian Alan polity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Alans' Iberian settlement zone is broadly indicated by ancient sources, but their exact territorial boundary—they were occupiers rather than administrators—cannot be reconstructed with cartographic precision.
